Definition: The non-proprietary name of the drug investigated in the trial. Must match the Generic_Name in the Drugs sheet for entity consistency.
The official name or acronym of the trial as cited in regulatory documents. Often used as the primary label for the trial in KG queries.
Indicates if the trial specifically investigates a treatment for Multiple Myeloma. Use "No" for all other diseases regardless of the specific cancer type.

The unique identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov. Vital for linking the KG to external public clinical trial registries.
Defines the clinical weight of the trial in the drug's regulatory package. Context like "Phase 3" or "Historical" must be placed in Notes.

Controlled_Values: Efficacy and safety | Safety only | PK/PD | HRQoL | Biomarker | Not reported
Definition: The primary objective of the study as designed. Most regulatory trials for oncology drugs will be "Efficacy and safety".

Definition: The clinical phase of development. Normalize numeric entries (e.g., "3" to "Phase 3") and combined phases (e.g., "12" to "Phase 1/2").
The level of masking used in the study to prevent bias. Populated from the study design section of the protocol or label.
Indicates if participants were assigned to study arms using a randomization process.
The ratio used for participant assignment to study arms. Enter "Not applicable" for non-randomized single-arm studies.

Controlled_Values: Interventional | Observational | Expanded access | Not reported
Definition: The high-level study design category. Most regulatory submissions will be "Interventional".
The total number of patients enrolled/randomized in the trial as an integer. Use "Not reported" if the final N is unknown.
Brief description of the trial participants, including disease state and prior treatment history.
Summary of the primary criteria required for trial entry. Focus on disease stage and molecular markers.
Example: Histologically confirmed Stage III or IV melanoma

Definition: Summary of criteria that disqualified patients from the trial. Focus on comorbidities or prior specific therapies.
The control arm used in the trial. Identify if it was placebo, active control, or standard of care.
The main outcome measure used to evaluate the trial's success.
Indicates if the trial achieved statistical significance for its primary endpoint(s).
The numerical result for the primary endpoint, such as Hazard Ratio (HR) or median months.
List of all other endpoints measured in the trial as specified in the protocol.
Example: Overall survival, ORR, Duration of response

Definition: The specific secondary endpoint given the most weight in regulatory discussions (often Overall Survival).
Flag indicating if Patient-Reported Outcomes were measured at any point during the trial.

Controlled_Values: Primary | Secondary | Exploratory | N/A | Not reported

Indicates if a Minimal Important Difference (MID) or Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) was predefined for the PRO instruments.
The total number of distinct PRO instruments used in the trial as an integer. Enter 0 if PROs were not assessed.
The main PRO tool used if one was prioritized, or the list of instruments if all were equal.
The timeline and frequency of PRO data collection. Important for assessing data density and potential for missingness.
The number of patients who completed the PRO assessment at the baseline visit.
Record the percentage or proportion of baseline PRO completion exactly as reported in the source.
The rate of missing PRO data over the course of the study or at specific milestones.
The percentage of expected PRO forms actually completed by patients.

The Digital Object Identifier for the main trial publication. Facilitates direct lookup of source data.
The 4-digit year the primary trial results were published.
Additional trial context, including specific PRO sub-domain results or regulatory nuances.
Example: Significant improvement in HRQoL noted in EPAR but not FDA label.

Definition: Unique composite identifier linking a specific trial to a specific instrument (e.g., TRIAL001INST01). Serves as the primary key for this sheet.
Foreign key linking to the Trial sheet. Used to identify which clinical study the instrument data belongs to.
Foreign key linking to the Drugs sheet. Used to identify the therapeutic agent associated with these instrument results.
The formal name of the Patient-Reported Outcome tool used in the trial. Should be consistent with established instrument nomenclature (e.g., EORTC QLQ-C30).

Definition: The primary construct or area of health being measured by the instrument. If an instrument covers multiple areas equally, use "Mixed".
List of specific sub-domains or scales within the instrument that were analyzed and reported.
A narrative summary of the main result for this instrument within the trial. Include whether the result was positive, negative, or neutral.
Example: Significant improvement in global health status vs comparator.

Definition: The hierarchical status of the instrument's findings within the trial's statistical hierarchy. Do not use a "PRO" suffix.

Controlled_Values: Favours intervention | Favours control | No significant difference | Mixed | Not reported
Definition: Indicates which treatment arm showed better outcomes according to this specific instrument.
Indicates if the observed change or difference between groups met the predefined Minimal Important Difference threshold.

The reported effect size (e.g., Cohen's d, Odds Ratio) for the instrument within the treatment group.
The difference in effect sizes or the net treatment effect between the intervention and control arms.
Detailed results or scores for each individual subscale reported for the instrument.

List of specific subscales that failed to reach statistical significance.
The number of patients who completed this specific instrument at the baseline assessment. May be lower than Trial_Enrollment_Total.
The proportion of patients who completed this instrument at baseline. Record exactly as reported (e.g., 0.913).
The reported rate of missing data specifically for this instrument over the study duration.
The compliance rate (actual vs. expected completions) for this specific instrument.
